spiritual_reading.full_translation: The Divine set governing order within clear wisdom, fixing authority in what had already gone forth from inward will into determinate expression. But when the leading falsity is forcibly restrained so it can no longer act or persuade, the dependent powers that had taken their coherence from it are torn apart and lose their joined operation. Yet even then, within what remains, there persists a limited capacity for order by which restoration can still be received and begun.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: it moves from the establishment of Divine rule in wisdom to the consequences of restraining a dominant falsity, ending with a remnant of recoverable order.
paragraph_translations.notes: The final clause about a remaining "measure of order" is clear as a remnant principle, but the exact mode and subject of that remnant is not fully determinate from the surviving wording.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a compact teaching: Divine authority is established in enlightened discernment; when a chief falsity is silenced, its associated faculties collapse; nevertheless a remnant capacity for order remains that can serve restoration. The only stumble is the last phrase, whose grammatical subject is uncertain, though its spiritual force as a remaining receptivity for re-ordering holds.

findings.diagnosis: Despite heavy damage, the paragraph reads as a single compact correspondential teaching: (1) establishment of a throne/command in light (order grounded in illumination and uttered word), (2) the muzzling/silencing of an acting agent, (3) the dismemberment/cutting-off of dependent parts, and (4) a remaining ‘measure of order.’ The spiritual reading’s only ‘stumble’ (uncertain subject of the remnant clause) is best explained by physical loss/fragmentation, not by an inserted administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: Text is visibly lacunose and garbled: “For [he established] … his [thro]ne in the light, which [and set]hich he had also uttered [as a word of command.] When that one will be muzzled, they shall [be cut off] cut limb [from them,] there is [s]till a [measure of order]”. The reader reports: “The only stumble is the last phrase, whose grammatical subject is uncertain,” which matches the broken syntax and bracketed restorations (“which [and set]hich…”, “cut off] cut limb”). Nothing here introduces jurisdictions, ranked lists, named rulers, stations, or inventory-style administration; the movement is processual (establish → muzzle → dismember → remnant). Removing any part would not improve voice consistency; it would only worsen an already-fragmentary causal chain.

findings.diagnosis: Positive confirmation: no evidence of Mani-style seam expansion or administrative insertion. The imagery (‘throne in the light,’ ‘word of command,’ ‘muzzled,’ ‘cut limb’) is internally cohesive and can be read functionally (correspondentially) as order-by-light/utterance, then restraint, then the collapse of coordinated members, then residual order.
findings.evidence: The paragraph lacks the signature markers of administrative voice (titles, authorities distributed over territories, enumerated ranks). Instead it uses functional/action verbs and state change: “established… throne in the light… uttered… word of command… muzzled… cut limb… still… measure of order.” This is exactly the kind of sequence the spiritual reading could narrate without forcing in external personnel or bureaucratic structures; its difficulty is grammatical (damage), not conceptual.

textual_criticism.summary: 2 findings: (1) the only stumbling point is due to damage/lacunae affecting syntax at the final clause (recommendation: none); (2) the surviving material is a coherent correspondential teaching with no administrative overlay or seam-expansion indicators (recommendation: none). No excisions or annotations are warranted on textual-voice grounds.
